text:
**For most people, LiFePO4 (also called LFP) is the better choice.** Several of the guides in your results reach the same conclusion. One says all 54 power stations in its data set use LiFePO4 ([Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). Another says LFP is the better buy for most people ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)).

| | LiFePO4 (LFP) | NMC |
|---|---|---|
| **Cycle life** | About 3,000–6,000 cycles | About 1,000–2,000 cycles |
| **Safety** | More thermally stable and less prone to thermal runaway | Fine when well built, but less tolerant of heat and abuse |
| **Weight and size** | Heavier and bulkier | About 20% lighter per Wh ([PowerStationMatch](https://powerstationmatch.com/learn/lifepo4-vs-nmc)) |
| **Upfront price** | Now usually similar or lower per Wh | Was cheaper, but the gap has mostly closed |
| **Cold weather** | Charging below freezing can be limited unless the unit has a heater | Handles cold somewhat better |
| **Lifespan** | Often 10+ years of regular use | Capacity fades sooner with heavy use |

**Choose LiFePO4 if:**
- You want a unit for home backup, outages, RV or van use, or regular off-grid use.
- You'll cycle it often and want it to last for years.
- Safety matters to you, for example if it's stored indoors.

**Consider NMC only if:**
- You need the lightest possible unit for backpacking, travel, or carrying it often.
- You'll use it rarely, so cycle life doesn't matter.
- You find a much better price on a specific model.

**Tips:**
- Check the spec sheet for the chemistry and the rated cycles, such as "3,500 cycles to 80%". Don't rely on the marketing page.
- Most major brands have moved their current models to LiFePO4, so you may not find many NMC options.
- If you'll charge in freezing conditions, look for a unit with low-temperature charging protection or a heater.
